# Grammar fixture: one real IRC line per case, byte-exact, CRLF in the file.
#
# **Each line after the `#` header is `<wire line> ||| <what podssh must
# believe about it>`.** The split is three pipes because a wire line may
# contain any character except CRLF, and a one-pipe split would break on a
# message that quotes one.
#
# **These are recorded lines, not invented ones.** Down to `# Captured`,
# they are the shapes RFC 2812 §2.3, §3 and §6 specify and that public
# ircds emit, and none of them is a measurement. The lines after
# `# Captured` are measurements of real servers, byte for byte.
#
# **`grammar.txt` proves the parser against a table. It does not prove the
# session** — a frame boundary landing mid-message cannot be written in this
# format at all, which is why `reassembly.rs` splits the bytes itself.

:irc.example.org 001 alice :Welcome to the Example IRC Network alice!u@h ||| a server prefix with a text that itself contains `alice!u@h`; the prefix is irc.example.org
:irc.example.org 005 alice CHANTYPES=# PREFIX=(ov)@+ NETWORK=Example CHANMODES=eIbq,k,flj,CFLMPQScgimnprstz CHANNELLEN=64 NICKLEN=12 MAXTARGETS=4 CASEMAPPING=ascii :are supported by this server ||| 005 with six tokens; the first parameter is the nick and is not a token
:alice!u@host PRIVMSG #ops :hello there world ||| a trailing is one parameter even with spaces in it
:alice!u@host PRIVMSG bob :see 12:30 for the handover ||| a colon inside the trailing is content
:alice!u@host PRIVMSG #c : ||| an empty trailing is a message, not a missing one
:bob!u@h.example NOTICE alice :you are being tested ||| a NOTICE carries a target and a trailing like a PRIVMSG
:alice!u@host JOIN #one,#two ||| two channels in one JOIN
:alice!u@host PART #one :bye now ||| PART with a reason
:alice!u@host TOPIC #one :the new topic ||| TOPIC with a topic
:alice!u@host NAMES #one ||| NAMES with one channel
:alice!u@host LIST ||| LIST with no parameters at all
:alice!u@host MODE #one +nt ||| MODE target plus a flag string
:alice!u@host QUIT :Client Quit ||| QUIT with a reason
PING :aBcD1234 ||| a PING token introduced by a colon
PING 12345 ||| a PING token with no colon
PONG :aBcD1234 ||| the PONG that answers the PING above, byte for byte
:alice!u@host NICK alicia ||| a nick change
USER alice 0 * :Alice Example ||| USER has five parameters and the third is <unused>
CAP * LS :multi-prefix sasl znc.in/self-message ||| a server CAP LS with capabilities in the trailing
CAP * ACK :znc.in/self-message ||| the server granting one capability
CAP * NAK :multi-prefix ||| the server refusing one capability
@+draft/shield=please;room :alice!u@host PRIVMSG #c :tagged ||| two tags, one with a value and one without
@room :alice!u@host PRIVMSG #c :valueless tag ||| a valueless tag
:alice!u@host AWAY :gone for lunch ||| an unknown command, kept whole
:alice!u@host ACCOUNT alice ||| an unknown command with a middle parameter
@time=2026-10-02T00:00:00.000Z :irc.example.org 376 alice :End of /MOTD command. ||| a tag before a server prefix before a numeric
:irc.example.org 433 * alice :Nickname is already in use ||| 433 during registration
:alice!u@host PRIVMSG #c :PODSSH1|offer|t1|file.bin|1000|4 ||| a file-transfer offer is an ordinary PRIVMSG

# Captured on 2026-10-10 (T-094) from three servers, each on the loopback
# of the build image, with clients that sent each form with and without
# the colon of its last parameter: ngircd 27, ergo 2.18.0 and InspIRCd
# 4.11.0. The last parameter comes either way, as each server chooses.
:pa!~pa@127.0.0.1 JOIN :#t ||| ngircd 27: the channel of a JOIN as the trailing
:pa!pa@127.0.0.1 JOIN :#t ||| InspIRCd 4.11.0: the channel of a JOIN as the trailing
:pa!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc JOIN #t ||| ergo 2.18.0: the channel of a JOIN as a middle
:pa!~pa@127.0.0.1 NICK :pa2 ||| ngircd 27: the new nick as the trailing
:pa!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc NICK pa2 ||| ergo 2.18.0: the new nick as a middle
:pa!~pa@127.0.0.1 TOPIC #t :newtopic ||| ngircd 27: the topic as the trailing
:pa!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc TOPIC #t newtopic ||| ergo 2.18.0: the topic as a middle
:pb!~pb@127.0.0.1 PART #t :bye ||| ngircd 27: the reason of a PART as the trailing
:pb!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc PART #t bye ||| ergo 2.18.0: the reason of a PART as a middle, not a second channel
:pa2!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc QUIT Quit ||| ergo 2.18.0: the reason of a QUIT as a middle
:pb!~u@mcevjy93nmghu.irc QUIT :Quit: done ||| ergo 2.18.0: the reason of a QUIT as the trailing
:pa!~pa@127.0.0.1 MODE #t +k secret ||| ngircd 27: a channel's key as a middle
:pa!pa@127.0.0.1 MODE #t +k :secret ||| InspIRCd 4.11.0: a channel's key as the trailing
:pa2!~pa@127.0.0.1 MODE pa2 :+i ||| ngircd 27: a user's mode as the trailing
:pa!~pa@127.0.0.1 PRIVMSG #t :word ||| ngircd 27: a PRIVMSG sent as PRIVMSG #t word arrives with its colon
:ergo.test 332 pc #t newtopic ||| ergo 2.18.0: the topic of 332 as a middle
:irc.inspircd.test 333 pc #t pa :1791604586 ||| InspIRCd 4.11.0: the time of 333 as the trailing
:irc.ngircd.test 333 pc #t pa 1791604412 ||| ngircd 27: the time of 333 as a middle
:ergo.test 221 pa +Zi ||| ergo 2.18.0: a user's modes as a middle of 221
ERROR Quit ||| ergo 2.18.0: the text of ERROR as a middle, an unknown command kept whole
:irc.ngircd.test PONG irc.ngircd.test :tok123 ||| ngircd 27: the answer to PING :tok123, the server and then the token as the trailing
:irc.inspircd.test PONG irc.inspircd.test :tok123 ||| InspIRCd 4.11.0: the answer to PING :tok123, the server and then the token as the trailing
:ergo.test PONG ergo.test tok123 ||| ergo 2.18.0: the answer to PING :tok123, the server and then the token as a middle
